questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
That they had a theatre-program, so that I would study something that I thought I could use in my career. 
That they spoke a language that I already knew, so that I wouldn't have a disadvantage socially with my new classmates.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. The University of Agder have a lot of exchange students, so they have a lot of detailed information on their website.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
A lot. 
The university made groups for the exchange students that were guided by local students. That way we had a secure base before we found new friends. 
I also had a meeting with a teater from the art-faculty, who introduced me and the other exchange students at this faculty to our building and teachers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Difficult. We were a lot of exchange students, so they didn't have room for all of us. 
The University also made a mistake, which caused me to not have access to the application system for the student housing before it was to late.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
That they need to get a monthly bus card. If you go to the city, you can buy a student one, which is the cheapest option. 
Also, that it can actually be more fun to live a lot of people together in a big house, than alone in you're own student apartment. Try make a deal with an Airbnb about a long-term stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It was difficult and there was a lot of steps. Take it one thing at a time, make lists and write down deadlines in your calendar to make it easier. 
The closer you are to home, the easier the proces will be, as the culture of the institutions and governments are more similar.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
As soon as I was accepted to the university it was easier. 
When we arrived we got a lot of help with signing up for classes, getting our student ID etc. It was a lot easier, when we were physically there.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They have a global-lounge with people always ready to assist you. That is the fastest way to get help – the office can be a bit slow in replying to your e-mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
I ended up with the classes I wanted, which was great. 
They did though make a mistake in my acceptance (said I wasn't qualified to take a theatre course). It took some time to fix the mistake, which was unfortunate and made it very stressful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you are qualified for the courses that you apply for – they say that they "recommend" some qualifications, but what they really mean is that you need them to be accepted.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I loved it. As a student in the creative field it was amazing to have a practical course with focus on my own work as an artist and not as an academic.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
The levels were fine. 
Some things were easier and some were more challenging.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more practical. A bit less structured.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Physical Theatre and Theatre Space + Communication, Media and Planning.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Anything in the art-department!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I already knew that Norway is an expensive country, so nothing really came as a surprise. Maybe the price of alcohol – especially at restaurants.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Books for classes were a bit more expensive than I thought. I was prepared for everything to be a bit more expensive though.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had a lot of different clubs. I participated in a choir, which was okay, but I didn't really feel completely a part of it as I had to leave in the end of the semester.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Outdoor activities, traditional sports, choir, student pub, quiz-night etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Quiz-night! So fun. 

Also ESN trips – we went to Preikestolen, which was an amazing experience even though it rained a lot.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Oslo, Bergen and Preikestolen. 
Some of the other exchange students also went further north in Norway, which was supposed to be really nice. 

Kristiansand also have some amazing escape-rooms, which are definitely worth a visit, and a cinema-club called "Cinemateket". For concerts go to Vaktbua, for theatre go to Kilden.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. There were small differences, but Norway and Denmark is very similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Invite them over to your place. Say yes, to everything you're invited to.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find anything challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor activities because of the country's nature and their traditions during Christmas time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) To have a class or a regular social activity with the locals, makes it easier to make norwegian friends. I was lucky to be the only exchange student in my class.
2) This is a semester of "yes" – Say yes to every offer you get, be open to new impressions and experiences. 
3) Prioritise activities with new friends instead of big group-tours.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not that I can think of.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Becoming friends with both locals and other exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting to experience as much of the country and the culture as possible while also prioritizing school.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
